# Art handover: characters and environments

A guide for iterating on the character and environment art of "Until there were none" (a Playdate horde shooter in
Zig) without breaking the game. Read it all before changing anything. `AGENTS.md` has the full project reference;
this file is the art contract.

**The short version:** all art is generated by Python scripts at final size, in 1-bit. The game reads frame layouts,
cell sizes and anchors from generated Zig files (`src/bitmap_descs.zig`, `src/kit_descs.zig`). So you can freely change
**how things look** inside the existing layouts. Changing **how many frames, which order, what size or where the feet
are** is a code change with knock-on effects. Each section below says which is which.

---

## 1. The target

| | |
|---|---|
| Screen | 400 x 240 px, **1-bit** (black and white only), reflective LCD, 50 FPS target |
| Scale | 128 px = 1 m. The view is about 3.1 x 1.9 m |
| Camera | Top-down 3/4 view (seen from above and slightly in front). Never mix in side or true top-down views |
| Light | From the **top left**, everywhere. Top faces lightest, front faces mid, cast shadows fall down and to the right |
| Tones | Five, through one ordered **4x4 Bayer** dither: white, light (25% black), mid (50%), dark (75%), black. No error diffusion (it crawls when things move) |
| Flicker | The view scrolls 1 px at a time, and on this LCD any pixel that flips reads as flicker. A single pixel checker flips *every* pixel on a 1 px move; a solid area only flips along its outline. So every kit is drawn in **phase variants** (next row), which keeps its fine shading still on screen. A kit left out of `DITHERED_KITS` falls back to the **solid** style: lit faces white, shadow faces and cast shadows solid black, detail in black or white lines, and dither (50%, in 2 x 2 pixel clusters, `DITHER_CELL`) only as small accents. Never use 12.5% fills, and keep the ground quiet line work either way. Measure: shift a level preview (`convert_tilemaps.py --preview logs`) by 1 px and count the flipped pixels: 3-7% of the screen now (single pixel dither was 11-17%) |
| Phase variants | The other way to keep fine dithering: draw the art in **phase variants** (`PHASES` in `env_kits.py`; every kit in `DITHERED_KITS`, currently all three). Each piece and the kit's levels' floors are rendered four times, once per screen pixel phase (x even/odd, y even/odd), and the renderer draws the version whose dither lines up with the screen, so the pattern stays still while the shapes move (3-4% flips, like the solid style). Rules: single pixel dither (`cell=1`), only the 25/50/75% tones (`LIGHT`, `MID`, `DARK`: they repeat every 2 px; anything finer needs 16 versions), dithered shadows with `p.dshadow`. Costs 4x the bitmaps per kit (each level's floors are about 600 KB in memory, 1.8 MB for the three) and nothing per frame |
| Contrast order | Characters (highest) > obstacles > ground (quietest). Ground is white with sparse detail. Each kit leans one way for identity: woods black foliage with white lit edges, city white concrete with black burnt vehicles, quarantine dark canvas with white markings |
| Grid | Level cells are **57 x 27 px** (0.445 x 0.211 m). Levels are 16 x 20 cells |
| Characters | Hero cell 48 x 48 (about 41 px tall on screen), zombies 32 to 64 px cells |

Dithered art is authored at **final size**. Never dither and then resize (it turns to mud), and never ship anything
that needs processing at runtime.

---

## 2. Rules that keep the game working

1. **Edit the scripts, not the PNGs.** Everything in `images/` and `levels/`, and `src/bitmap_descs.zig` /
   `src/kit_descs.zig`, is generated and gets overwritten. The source of the art is the Python scripts.
2. **Frame layouts are a contract with the code.** Sheet names, frame order, frame counts, cell sizes and anchors are
   read by `src/animation.zig` and `src/renderer.zig`. Keep them unless you also make the code change (section 9).
3. **Feet are the anchor.** Every character and obstacle is depth-sorted and placed by its feet/base pixel. If the
   feet move inside the cell, the sprite floats or sinks and sorts wrongly.
4. **Only facings 0 to 180 degrees are drawn; the game mirrors the rest.** Character models must be left/right
   symmetric, with weapons held two-handed in the middle. Anything one-sided (a holster, a sign, text) flips when
   mirrored.
5. **Environment piece lists are append-only.** A piece's index in its kit is its tile id in every Tiled map and every
   level file. Inserting, removing or reordering silently swaps art *and collision* in every level. Add new pieces at
   the end. To retire one, leave it in place and stop using it.
6. **A piece's footprint is its collision.** Changing `fw`/`fh` changes which cells block movement and bullets in
   every level that uses it. The drawn base must sit on the footprint.
7. **Gameplay sizes come from the hero cell.** Collision radii, melee range and pickup radii derive from `CHAR_W`
   (48). Don't change the hero cell size for looks.
8. **No new runtime work.** No per-pixel drawing, recolouring or resampling in the game. More/larger sprites cost
   frame time on a 168 MHz CPU with a 4 KB data cache.

---

## 3. Pipeline map

| Script | Draws | Writes | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `character_sprites.py` (uses `sdf_sprites.py`) | Hero body, hero gun and melee layers, 4 zombie kinds | `images/hero-table-*.png`, `hero_gun-*`, `hero_melee-*`, `zombie_<kind>-table-*` | `renderer.zig` (sheets), `animation.zig` (frame maths) |
| `gore_sprites.py` | Gibs (cut from the zombie models), blood pools and spatters | `images/gibs_<kind>-table-*`, `splats-*`, `spatters-*` | `renderer.zig`, `gore_system.zig`, `animation.zig` |
| `drop_sprites.py` | Ammo/health pickups (hand-authored pixel grids) | `images/drops-table-*` | `renderer.zig`, `animation.zig` |
| `env_kits.py` | Environment kits: pieces, ground art, decals, outside | `images/<kit>-piece-<n>.png`, `map-tiles/kits/*.tsx` + previews, `src/kit_descs.zig` | `renderer.zig`, `level_loader.zig`, `convert_tilemaps.py` |
| `convert_tilemaps.py` | Bakes each level's floor | `levels/<level>.bin`, `images/ground-<level>.png` | `level_loader.zig`, `renderer.zig` |
| `convert_raw.py <imagemagick>` | Runs all of the above, plus the launcher card | wipes `images/`, writes `src/bitmap_descs.zig` | everything |

Important: running `character_sprites.py`, `gore_sprites.py` or `drop_sprites.py` on their own rewrites their images
only. **`src/bitmap_descs.zig` is written only by `convert_raw.py`.** If you change any layout constant (frame counts,
cell sizes, anchors), you must run `convert_raw.py` (needs ImageMagick, takes minutes because of the character
render), then `zig fmt src`.

`env_kits.py` writes `src/kit_descs.zig` itself; run `convert_tilemaps.py` after it so the levels' baked floors pick
up ground, decal and outside changes.

---

## 4. Characters (`character_sprites.py`)

Models are built from primitives (ellipsoids, capsules, boxes) and ray-cast to 1-bit by `sdf_sprites.py` with two-tone
cel shading, part lines, a black outline and (hero only) a white rim. The header of the script documents the sheets.

### Sheet contract

Index = `facing * frames_per_facing + frame`, facing = degrees / step, facing 0 = towards the screen, 90 = screen
left, 180 = away.

| Sheet | Cell (w x h, feet x, y) | Facings | Frames per facing | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hero` | 48 x 48, feet (24, 43) | 19 (every 10 degrees) | 6: idle, run 0-3, hurt | 114, then death |
| `hero` death (from index `HERO_DEATH_START` = 114) | same | 5 (every 45 degrees) | 4 falling frames | 20 (134 total) |
| `hero_gun` | same cell and anchor as `hero` | 19 | 2: idle, hurt | 38 |
| `hero_melee` | same | 19 | 3: ready, strike, follow-through | 57 |
| `zombie_runner` | 32 x 32, feet (16, 29) | 11 (every 18 degrees) | 5: walk 0-3, hit | 55 |
| `zombie_walker` | 48 x 48, feet (24, 43) | 11 | 5 | 55 |
| `zombie_shambler` | 48 x 48, feet (24, 43) | 11 | 5 | 55 |
| `zombie_brute` | 64 x 64, feet (32, 58) | 11 | 5 | 55 |

- The hero is two draw items in the same cell: the body (`hero`), then the arms and weapon (`hero_gun` or
  `hero_melee`) drawn straight over it with the same anchor. The body's occlusion of the arms is baked into the
  weapon layer (pixels the body hides are left out). Keep the body free of arms.
- Zombie kinds are in `EnemyKind` order: runner, walker, shambler, brute (`ENEMY_CELLS` follows that order).
- Zombies have **no death frames**: they burst into gibs.
- The run/walk cycles are stepped by distance travelled (`HERO_RUN_CYCLE_DIST` 0.4 m, `ENEMY_WALK_CYCLE_DIST` 0.35 m).
  Draw a cycle that reads at those strides.
- The gun's barrels are at `GUN_Z` / `GUN_MUZZLE_Y` in the script, matched by `GUN_HEIGHT_PX` (12) and
  `MUZZLE_FORWARD` (0.14 m) in `tweak_constants.zig`: bullets are drawn leaving the muzzle there. Move the gun and you
  must update both.

### Safe to change (no code change)

- Shapes, proportions, clothing, tones, outlines, shading, dither choice, part lines: anything inside the cell that
  keeps the feet on the anchor pixel and the body inside the cell.
- Poses within the existing frame slots (a better run cycle, a punchier hurt frame).
- The look of each zombie kind, as long as kinds stay distinguishable at a glance (silhouette and size first). Gibs
  are cut from these models, so re-run `gore_sprites.py` afterwards (section 5).

### Needs a code change (or at least `convert_raw.py`)

- Frame counts, facing steps, frame order, new animations (for example an attack swing for zombies): change the
  constants in the script **and** the frame maths in `src/animation.zig` (`heroFrame`, `heroWeaponFrame`,
  `heroDeathFrame`, `enemyFrame`) and its tests. Facing steps must divide 180.
- Cell sizes or feet anchors: regenerate `bitmap_descs.zig` via `convert_raw.py`. Larger cells cost draw time.
  Changing the hero cell changes gameplay sizes (rule 7).
- A new zombie kind or sheet: new `EnemyKind` in `game_state.zig`, tuning in `ENEMY_KINDS` (`tweak_constants.zig`),
  sheet lists in `renderer.zig` (`Sheet`, `SHEET_FILES`), gibs in `gore_sprites.py`. That is a gameplay change, not an
  art change.

Check: `python character_sprites.py images --preview logs/characters.png` (a few minutes) writes the tables and a
contact sheet.

---

## 5. Gore (`gore_sprites.py`)

- `gibs_<kind>`: index = `(fade * GIB_PARTS + part) * GIB_SPIN_FRAMES + frame`. 4 fade levels (solid, then thinning)
  x 5 parts (head, arm, leg, torso, chunk) x 8 spin frames = 160 frames. Square cells (`GIB_CELLS`: runner 20,
  walker 28, shambler 28, brute 48), the piece centred.
- `splats` (pools): 4 large + 4 medium variants x 3 fades, 56 x 32 cells, centred. `spatters`: 4 variants x 3 fades,
  12 x 8.
- Gibs are cut from the zombie models by tag (`GIB_TAGS`), so they follow character changes automatically; if you rename
  or restructure a zombie's parts, update `GIB_TAGS`.
- Blood is black. Fades are dither thinning, so keep fade frames as true subsets of the solid frame.

Check: `python gore_sprites.py images --preview logs/gore.png` (seconds).

---

## 6. Pickups (`drop_sprites.py`)

- Hand-authored grids (`B` black, `W` white, `d` 75% dither, `l` 25% dither, `.` clear), each character drawn 2 x 2,
  plus a 1 px white rim added at final size.
- Table `drops`: per kind (ammo_small, ammo_large, health_small, health_large, in that order) a still frame then 5
  glint frames: 6 frames per kind, 24 total. Cells 48 x 42, the sprite bottom-centred (the bottom row is the base).
- Type reads by tone (ammo dark with brass on top, health a white kit with a black cross), size by footprint. Large
  ones are only a little bigger than small ones on purpose: keep them smaller than the hero.
- The renderer draws a ground shadow under each drop (`DROP_SHADOW_W`/`_LARGE` in `renderer.zig`) and the pickup
  radii are in `tweak_constants.zig` (`DROP_PICKUP_RADIUS*`); keep them in step with the drawn size.

Check: `python drop_sprites.py` (instant).

---

## 7. Environment kits (`env_kits.py`)

Three kits: `woods`, `city`, `quarantine`. Each kit has:

- **pieces**: obstacles placed on a level's `objects` layer. Each is one bitmap and has a **footprint** (`fw` x `fh`
  cells) that blocks movement and bullets.
- **ground**: flat art for a level's `ground` layer (paths, roads, tracks, helipad). Never blocks. Baked into the
  floor bitmap and dithered once across the whole level, so neighbouring cells line up.
- **decals**: tiny ground details (tufts, cracks, casings) scattered over free floor by a hash of the cell
  (`decal_chance` per cell). Baked.
- **outside**: a function that fills the view beyond the map's edge (it is visible: the camera isn't clamped). Baked.

### Drawing conventions

- Pieces are drawn in **local pixel coordinates** with a `Pen`: the footprint covers x `0 .. fw*57-1` and y
  `-fh*27 .. -1`. The **anchor** is the centre of the footprint's bottom-left cell, local `(28, -14)`: that is the
  object's world position and its depth for sorting.
- Draw the object's base inside the footprint, near the bottom of it. Overhangs (canopies, roofs, shadows) may extend
  outside it; they will overlap characters correctly through depth sorting.
- Footprints extend **right and up** from the cell the piece is placed on (like a Tiled tile).
- Use `p.shadow(...)` / `p.shadow_ellipse(...)` for cast shadows: solid black, down and to the right. `ink=True` on
  a shape makes only its black pixels opaque (for a dithered accent laid over the ground without white specks).
- **Border pieces** (the ring round each level: `facade_*` and `wall_side` in city, `fence_h`/`fence_v` in quarantine,
  trees and bushes in woods) must be exactly one cell wide with no side outline where they join, so a row reads as one
  wall or street.
- **Keep the bottom border row and the bottom of the outside low (about one row tall).** Tall things there hide the
  player near the bottom edge, and baked art that reaches up into the playfield is drawn under the characters.
- Mirroring: pieces can be flipped per placement in Tiled. The flipped anchor is computed (`anchor_x_flipped`), so
  flipping is free, but light then comes from the right on that copy: flip foliage and rubble, not buildings with
  strong shadows or text.

### Phase variants

- A kit built with `Kit(..., cell=1, phases=PHASES)` and its pieces with `Art(..., cell=1, phases=PHASES)` gets four
  bitmaps per piece (`<kit>-piece-<n>-p<v>.png`) and four floors per level (`ground-<level>-p<v>.png`); `kit_descs.zig`
  records `phases` and the renderer loads and picks them itself. Nothing else changes.
- `DITHERED_KITS` picks which kits use their fine dithered art in phase variants (`wd_*`, `cd_*`, `qd_*` pieces);
  the rest use the solid style (`w_*`, `c_*`, `q_*`, one bitmap per piece). Re-run `env_kits.py` and
  `convert_tilemaps.py` after changing it. Edit the style in use (both sets keep the same names, footprints and order).
- Characters, gore and drops are not in phase variants (yet), so their dither still moves with them.

### Safe to change (no code change)

- The drawing of any existing piece, ground art, decal or outside, keeping its footprint. Re-run
  `python env_kits.py images --preview logs/kits.png` then `python convert_tilemaps.py --preview logs` and look at
  `logs/level-<name>.png`.
- New pieces, ground art or decals **appended** to a kit's lists. To use them, place them in the `.tmx` maps (Tiled
  reads the regenerated tilesets in `map-tiles/kits/`).
- A new kit: add a `build_<kit>()` and append it to `KIT_BUILDERS`. Levels choose it with the map property `kit`.
  (Kit order is stored in level files as an index, so append kits too.)

### Needs care

- **Changing a footprint** changes collision in every level using the piece. Re-check the maps: run
  `python convert_tilemaps.py --preview logs` (it errors if a footprint now overlaps another piece or leaves the map)
  and make sure no path or drop point got sealed off.
- Limits: at most 127 pieces per kit (bit 7 of the level file's piece byte is the flip), at most 8 levels
  (`MAX_LEVELS` in `renderer.zig`).
- The baked floor extends `GROUND_MARGIN_X` (256) / `GROUND_MARGIN_Y` (160) px past the map, covering the camera's
  widest lean. Shrinking them shows white past the outside; growing them costs memory (each floor is about 150 KB).
- Cell size (57 x 27) is shared by the levels, the converter and the game. Don't change it from the art side.

---

## 8. Levels and how art plugs in

- Maps are `map-tiles/<level>.tmx` (Tiled, 57 x 27 px tiles, 16 x 20 cells), read directly by
  `convert_tilemaps.py`. Layers: `ground` (the kit's `<kit>_ground` tileset), `objects` (`<kit>_pieces`), and a
  `drops` object layer with points named `small`, `large` and one `start`.
- Tiled shows previews cropped to the footprint; the game draws the full bitmap.
- Layout is a level design job (`.claude/skills/level-designer/SKILL.md`). An art change should not need a layout
  change unless a footprint changed.

---

## 9. Budgets and hard limits

- **Frame index is a `u8`**: no sheet may exceed 256 frames (hero is 134, gibs 160).
- **Draw list**: every visible sprite is an 8-byte record sorted each frame; it is kept inside half the 4 KB data
  cache. Fewer, larger sprites beat many tiny ones. At 100 enemies about 100 sprites are drawn.
- **Overdraw and draw calls** cost more than maths on device. Avoid big mostly-transparent bitmaps: transparency still
  stores a mask (1-bit image + 1-bit mask).
- **Memory**: all kit pieces and every level's floor are loaded at startup (currently 37 pieces x 4 phases = 148
  bitmaps, and three levels x 4 phases of ~150 KB floors, about 1.8 MB). Keep pieces trimmed (the script trims to
  what is drawn).
- **50 FPS on the device is the bar**, and the simulator hides performance problems. Anything that adds sprites,
  enlarges cells or adds sheets needs a device FPS check at worst case.

---

## 10. Checking your work

Run from the repo root (Windows; see `AGENTS.md` for the toolchain):

1. Regenerate what you changed:
   - characters: `python character_sprites.py images --preview logs/characters.png`
   - gore: `python gore_sprites.py images --preview logs/gore.png`
   - drops: `python drop_sprites.py`
   - environment: `python env_kits.py images --preview logs/kits.png` then `python convert_tilemaps.py --preview logs`
   - any layout constant changed: `python convert_raw.py <imagemagick path>` (everything, minutes)
2. `zig fmt src build.zig`
3. `zig build test --summary all` (frame maths tests catch index overruns) and `zig build` plus
   `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSmall` (the device build).
4. Look at it in the game at 1:1 (zoomed previews lie): `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File
   tools/sim.ps1 -Invincible -Level woods` (or `city`, `quarantine`), then read `logs/screenshot.png`. Drive it with
   `tools/sim-input.ps1` (see `AGENTS.md`). Check: silhouettes read, characters pop over the ground, the player is
   hidden behind tall pieces only when behind them, no dither seams, nothing floats or sinks, both mirrored halves
   look right.
5. A game panic shows in `logs/sim-stderr.log` (for example a bitmap index out of range when a sheet has fewer frames
   than the code expects).
6. Contrast, ghosting and frame rate must finally be judged on a real Playdate.

---

## 11. Don't touch from the art side

- `src/bitmap_descs.zig`, `src/kit_descs.zig`, `levels/*.bin`, `images/*` (generated).
- The order of `EnemyKind`, `DropKind`, kit lists, piece lists and ground lists (append only).
- `CELL_W`/`CELL_H`, `ANCHOR_LOCAL`, the hero cell size `HERO_W`/`HERO_H` and its anchor, facing steps and frame counts,
  unless you are also changing the code that reads them (section 4).
- `build.zig`, `link_map.ld` and anything about the device build.
